title: Graceful stream truncation & offline tool queueing — SDK patterns (sketch)
content:
Purpose

This sketch proposes a lightweight set of SDK and protocol conventions to make hosted streaming usable for low-bandwidth or flaky clients and to enable safe, observable offline tool-calling. The goal is pragmatic: reduce incidents where client dropouts cause lost tool calls or invalid partial structured output, without adding heavy server-side state or breaking existing streaming flows.

Context and motivation

We see two recurring pain patterns from internal SDK support and customer logs: (1) interrupted streaming responses where the client never receives a final structured payload (JSON incomplete / trailing action frames missing), and (2) mobile/edge clients that must invoke tools (search, webfetch, DB write) but can be offline or throttled — leading to silent failures or poor UX. Current resumable proposals are heavyweight and require server pinning; we need a lower-friction approach that works with existing hosted API sessions.

High-level approach

- Streaming frames remain the canonical primitive; we add a small set of explicit frame types and idempotency tokens so clients + SDKs can recover.
- Clients expose a local offline tool queue in the SDK that serializes outbound tool requests with minimal metadata and retries to the server when network returns. Tool-calls include an idempotency-key and a short-lived proof that the server can validate (signed ticket or ephemeral session token) to avoid double execution on the backend.
- The server emits compact checkpoint frames with a resume_token every N logical frames (default N=8) and always emits a final checkpoint (or a terminal error frame) before closing the socket. If a client only receives earlier frames, the resume_token allows asking the server to replay from that checkpoint.

Design constraints

- Minimal server state: resume tokens are opaque and stateless on the server side (HMAC of last-processed-offset + expiry + model-version). Server can validate and replay from underlying logs without per-session memory.
- Backwards compatible: unchanged streaming payloads remain valid; new frame types are optional and ignored by older clients.
- Mobile-first: small resume tokens and compact frames to reduce bandwidth.

Wire primitives (stream frame sketch)

Each message over the stream is a newline-delimited JSON object (light framing). Frame envelope: {"ft": "<frame_type>", "id": "<frame_id>", "ts": <iso8601>, "p": <payload>}. Fields: ft = frame type short code, id = client-visible monotonic id, ts timestamp.

Frame types (ft):
- text: incremental text delta (p = {"delta": "..."})
- struct: partial structured output; p = {"path": "/items/0/summary", "json": <partial-json-string>} (partial JSON must be valid prefix of JSON value)
- action: tool call request emitted by model/device; p = {"tool": "search", "args": {...}, "call_id": "uuid-v4"}
- action_ack: server ack of action acceptance; p = {"call_id": "...", "status": "accepted|queued|failed", "exec_id": "r-1234"}
- checkpoint: {p: {"resume_token": "<base64>", "last_id": "<frame id>"}} — emitted every N frames and on close.
- terminal: final status with optional structured result pointer.

Resume token semantics

- Format: base64(HMAC(server_key, session_id || last_frame_id || model_version || expiry_ts) || last_frame_id || expiry_ts). Opaque to clients; server can verify HMAC and replay from last_frame_id in logs.
- Expiry: short (default 2 minutes) for low server memory; longer tokens permitted for dedicated enterprise customers via config.
- Replay endpoint: POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/replay with body {"resume_token": "...", "want_frames_after_id": "..."}. Server verifies token and streams frames from last_frame_id onward.

Partial structured output guidance

- Servers should prefer incremental JSON fragments that are always valid when appended (e.g., arrays of top-level items) or supply path-based partials (struct frames).
- Final structured payload must be referenced in terminal frame with a canonical retrieval URL or final frame containing the fully-validated JSON. If final frame not received, clients should attempt replay using nearest checkpoint token.

Client SDK: offline tool queueing (mobile/edge)

Goals: allow apps to accept user input while offline and reliably deliver tool calls once connectivity returns, without risking duplicate side-effects.

Local queue shape (persisted to disk): queue entry = {"call_id": "uuid", "tool": "name", "args": <json>, "idempotency_key": "sha256", "session_hint": "s-1234", "expiry": <iso>}. SDK exposes: enqueueToolCall(), drainQueue(), queryCallStatus(call_id).

Delivery protocol:
1) SDK POSTs tool call to server with Idempotency-Key header + body including call_id and session_hint.
2) Server responds 202 Accepted + call_receipt {"receipt_id": "r-...", "status_endpoint": "/tool/status/r-..."} and stores call as at-least-once. If the server detects call with same idempotency key, it returns previous receipt.
3) Once online, SDK drains queue and retries until it receives an action_ack with status accepted/queued/executed or until entry expiry.

Server-side protections:
- Idempotency layer keyed by idempotency_key with TTL (configurable). Attempted duplicate deliveries should be fast-returning and deterministic.
- Optional "signed ticket" model: when a streaming session emits an action frame that expects a downstream tool call, it contains a signed short-lived ticket (expiring in 30s) that the SDK can include with an offline delivery to prove the call originated from a model session. This prevents arbitrary replay of queued tool calls from other sources.

SDK ergonomics and APIs (surface)

- Streaming client: StreamReader(stream_url, opts)
  - opts: {prefer_resume: boolean, resume_token: string?, latency_budget_ms: int?, checkpoint_interval: int}
  - callbacks: onTextDelta(id, delta), onStructPartial(id, path, json_fragment), onActionRequest(id, tool, args), onCheckpoint(resume_token), onTerminal(status, result_url)
- Tool queue client: ToolQueue(storage_backend, opts)
  - methods: enqueue(call), startDrain(), stopDrain(), status(call_id)
  - events: onCallAck(call_id, receipt), onCallFinalized(call_id, result)

Developer ergonomics notes:
- Default SDK behavior should be conservative: do not auto-execute queued tool calls that perform destructive actions (writes) unless the app explicitly marks entry as safe-for-deferred-execute.
- Provide helpers to convert action frames into a user-confirmation flow (UI prompt) before enqueueing in offline mode.
- Expose a small test harness in SDK to simulate flaky networks and validate resume behavior.

Observability and SLOs

Key telemetry to emit and surface in Redwood Console:
- stream.checkpoint.emitted (count, per-model)
- stream.resume.attempts (count, success_rate)
- stream.resume.latency_ms (p50/95)
- stream.partial-termination.rate (sessions closed without terminal frame)
- toolqueue.drain.success_rate (per-client-platform)
- toolcall.duplicate-detected (counts where idempotency prevented replayed execution)

Dashboards: per-route charts for partial-termination.rate and resume success. Alert: partial-termination.rate > 0.5% for 5m for a route -> investigate SDK+client version.

Rollout plan (phased)

1) Internal dogfood (2 weeks): wire new frame types and resume tokens in internal staging; use two mobile apps and SDK integration tests; exercise simulated network dropouts.
2) Canary (4 weeks): enable opt-in header X-Enable-Resume: true for 1% of hosted-api traffic for specific routes. Monitor resume success and duplication metrics.
3) Opt-in SDK release: mobile SDK exposes resume APIs in beta; customers opt-in.
4) Gradual default-on: after 8–12 weeks, flip default behavior for SDKs and server for non-critical routes; keep opt-out for high-risk enterprise write operations.

Open questions / tradeoffs

- Server-side replay cost: stateless resume tokens simplify server memory but require log replay paths; what is the perf of log-based replay for high-throughput routes? (engineering to prototype.)
- Ticket model complexity: signed tickets solve replay abuse but add signing/verification ops; is simple idempotency-key TTL sufficient for most use cases?
- UX for destructive tool calls: should SDK block enqueue of destructive calls by default? (product decision)
- Cross-region resume: tokens tied to session-backed region may not work if traffic shifts; consider cross-region validation strategy for multi-region customers.

Action items (short term)

- Engineering: prototype checkpoint emission + resume endpoint (owner: Liam) — 2 sprints
- SDK: implement local ToolQueue draft with disk persistence and simple API (owner: Jessie) — 1 sprint
- Observability: add resume/checkpoint metrics and alert (owner: Samir) — 1 sprint
- Product: finalize enterprise token TTL config + opt-out matrix (owner: Rosa) — 2 weeks

Notes to reviewers

This is a lightweight, pragmatic sketch meant to be iterated quickly. Focus feedback on: (a) security model for offline tool delivery, (b) expected server replay costs for our busiest routes, and (c) SDK developer ergonomics for mobile. Avoid long-form API schema bikeshedding in this pass; we want to validate the pattern works end-to-end first.

References and related drafts

See linked artifacts above (GH#8742, JIRA-API-1297). Also related: "compact-transcript-schema-and-offline-tool-adaptor-brainstorm" and "resumable-partial-response-and-sdk-patterns-prd-draft" — this doc aims to be an alternative lighter path prioritizing mobile/offline UX.
